newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end up despite Victorias' troubles.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end up despite Victorias' troubles.

text.p: The Manila share index closed up on Friday despite concerns about exposure of several banks to sugar miller Victorias Milling Co which has sought a moratorium on its debts, traders said.

"There was an initial overreaction to the Victorias issue but now that the issue has been clarified, people see it's not as bad as it was rumoured to be," said Allan Araullo, vice-president at Regina Capital Development Corp.
Victorias, which on Thursday secured a moratorium on its 4.4 billion peso debt, ended 1.30 pesos lower, or down 28.89 percent, at 3.20 pesos.

Brokers said stocks of banks said to have exposure to Victorias fell. Metropolitan Bank fell 10 pesos to 685 and Bank of Philippine Islands fell one peso to 182. But Philippine National Bank reversed earlier losses by closing up 2.50 pesos at 307.50 pesos.
Jonas Ferrer, vice-president at Pryce Securities said investors saw reason to accumulate on index-linked issues like Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Ayala Land Inc and Ayala Corp.
Losers outpaced gainers 81 to 48 with 71 issues unchanged. Volume was still heavy at 18.7 billion shares valued at 4.1 billion pesos.
Oil, finance and mining sub-indices were down while commercial-industrials, property and all-share indices rose.

"The breadth of the market is still looking for direction and we would likely see the same sideways movement next week for lack of any other news," said Ramon Garcia, president at Diversified Securities Inc.
